# HTML response built from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/xss` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data written into an HTML response without escaping (Express, Fastify, Next.js,
Node's `http`): a string sent with `res.send()` (which Express answers as `text/html`),
`res.write()`/`res.end()` of visible HTML, and the bodies of Next.js API routes and route handlers
that answer with HTML. Request data that is escaped, sanitised, rendered through a template engine,
or sent as JSON is not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Markup in the value becomes part of the page. A value such as `<script>...</script>` runs in the
browser of everyone who opens the link or page: it can read what the user sees, act in their name
and steal data that scripts can reach.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the name goes into the HTML as it is.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

app.get('/hello', (req, res) => {
  res.send('<p>Hello, ' + req.query.name + '</p>');
});
```

**Compliant:** the name is escaped for HTML first.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const escapeHtml = require('escape-html');

const app = express();

app.get('/hello', (req, res) => {
  res.send('<p>Hello, ' + escapeHtml(req.query.name) + '</p>');
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Escape request data for HTML: `escapeHtml(x)` from `escape-html`, `he.escape(x)` or
  `validator.escape(x)`.
- For HTML that users may write, sanitise it with sanitize-html or DOMPurify.
- Render pages through an autoescaping template engine: `res.render(view, data)`.
- Where no HTML is meant, answer with JSON (`res.json(data)`) or set another content type first.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- Node.js http

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A content type set through an object of headers (`res.set({ 'Content-Type': ... })`) is not seen:
  a later `res.send()` of a string is taken for HTML.
- `res.write()`/`res.end()` without an HTML content type are checked only when the text is visibly
  HTML; a bare request value written without a content type is missed, although browsers may sniff
  it as HTML.
- Results of awaited calls on other objects (a database lookup by a request value) are taken for
  stored data.
- `res.send()` of a variable first assigned an object or array is taken for JSON, even if the
  variable later holds a string.
- A Fastify handler whose reply parameter is named `res` is taken for an Express handler, so a
  string it sends (plain text in Fastify) is reported.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

The test files [`rules/js/xss/xss.js`](../../../rules/js/xss/xss.js) and [`rules/js/xss/xss.ts`](../../../rules/js/xss/xss.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
